introduction: Don Pedro and his companions arrive in Messina after a successful military campaign and become guests of Leonato. Claudio quickly hopes to marry Leonato's daughter Hero, while Benedick and Beatrice renew a sharp, familiar exchange of insults. Their friends see an opportunity for matchmaking, but Don Pedro's resentful brother Don John looks for a way to spoil the happiness around him. As overheard conversations and arranged appearances shape the courtships, trust depends less on what is true than on whom people choose to believe.

fullSynopsis.text: Leonato welcomes Don Pedro, Claudio, Benedick and the recently reconciled Don John. Claudio falls in love with Hero, and Don Pedro offers to woo her for him at a masked entertainment. Benedick, meanwhile, trades insults with Beatrice and insists that he will remain a bachelor. An imperfectly overheard conversation leads Antonio to tell Leonato that Don Pedro wants Hero for himself. Don John learns the actual arrangement from Borachio and sees a chance to injure Claudio, whose success he resents. At the dance, he persuades the masked Claudio that Don Pedro has betrayed him by courting Hero on his own account.

Don Pedro clears up the suspicion: he has won Hero for Claudio with Leonato's consent, and their wedding is arranged. He then recruits Leonato, Claudio and Hero to make Benedick and Beatrice fall in love. Knowing Benedick is listening in the garden, the men invent an account of Beatrice's desperate secret passion and fear that he would mock her. Benedick believes them and resolves to return her love. Hero and Ursula stage a corresponding conversation for Beatrice, praising Benedick while condemning her own proud disdain. Beatrice also accepts what she overhears and determines to answer his supposed devotion with love.

Don John and Borachio devise a more destructive deception. Borachio will court Hero's attendant Margaret at her mistress's window, calling her Hero, while Don John brings Claudio and Don Pedro to watch. They expect the men to mistake Margaret for Hero and believe her unfaithful. Don John makes the accusation and offers apparent proof; Claudio resolves to disgrace Hero publicly if he sees it. That night, the Watch overhears Borachio telling Conrade that the trick has succeeded and arrests them both. Dogberry and Verges try to bring the matter before Leonato, but their confused, lengthy speech fails to convey its urgency before he leaves for the wedding.

At the church Claudio refuses Hero and denounces her as sexually dishonest, supported by Don Pedro and Don John. She denies their account and faints. Leonato initially accepts the accusations and turns against her, but Beatrice and Friar Francis believe her innocent; Benedick suspects Don John. The friar proposes concealing Hero and reporting her dead, hoping that apparent loss will turn slander into remorse and allow the truth to emerge. Benedick and Beatrice privately confess their love, but she demands action for Hero: he must kill Claudio. He finally agrees to challenge him. Elsewhere, the prisoners' examination establishes the false accusation, and the Sexton sets out to inform Leonato.

Leonato and Antonio confront Claudio and Don Pedro, who still defend their accusation. Benedick then challenges Claudio and breaks with their company. The Watch brings the prisoners, and Borachio confesses that they saw Margaret in Hero's clothes, not Hero. He also insists that Margaret did not knowingly participate in the plot. Claudio and Don Pedro offer penance, still believing Hero dead. Leonato requires public acknowledgment of her innocence, an epitaph and mourning at her tomb, and Claudio's marriage to a supposed niece who resembles her. Claudio accepts, then performs the memorial observance with music and vows to repeat it annually.

Claudio returns ready to marry the veiled niece, who reveals herself as Hero and affirms her innocence. The friar promises an explanation after the marriage rites. Benedick asks to marry Beatrice, but their familiar denials resume until their friends produce love poems written in their own hands. They agree to the match and kiss. Benedick abandons his quarrel with Claudio and insists on dancing before the weddings. A messenger reports that Don John has been captured while fleeing and brought back to Messina under guard. Benedick postpones thoughts of punishment until tomorrow, and the company ends in a dance with both marriages intended.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: A messenger announces Don Pedro's return from war with Claudio and Benedick. Beatrice's questions about Benedick prepare their renewed battle of wit when Leonato welcomes the visitors. Claudio admires Hero and hopes to marry her, while Benedick rejects both love and marriage. Don Pedro offers to court Hero in Claudio's name at the evening's masked festivities, then secure her father's consent. Antonio brings Leonato a mistaken report that the prince loves Hero himself, showing how easily overhearing can distort intentions. In contrast, Borachio learns the arrangement accurately and passes it to Don John. Although newly reconciled with his brother, Don John resents Claudio and begins looking for a way to obstruct the proposed marriage.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: At the masked dance, Beatrice wounds Benedick's pride with her description of him as the prince's jester. Don John and Borachio convince Claudio that Don Pedro is courting Hero for himself, but the prince resolves the misunderstanding by announcing that he has won her for Claudio. The wedding is set, and the friends plan another match between Beatrice and Benedick. Don John separately accepts Borachio's scheme to counterfeit Hero's infidelity using Margaret at her chamber window. In the garden, Balthasar sings about men's inconstancy before Don Pedro, Leonato and Claudio arrange to be overheard describing Beatrice's supposedly desperate love. Benedick trusts their performance and resolves to requite her, reading affection into her brusque invitation to dinner.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Hero and Ursula lure Beatrice into overhearing praise of Benedick and a story of his concealed love. Their criticism of her scorn leads her to resolve to love him in return. The men tease the newly altered Benedick, then Don John tells Claudio and Don Pedro that Hero is disloyal and invites them to witness apparent proof. Dogberry's confused instructions to the Watch are followed by an accidental discovery: Borachio boasts to Conrade about deceiving the noblemen with Margaret at Hero's window. The Watch arrests them. Hero prepares for her wedding amid teasing about Beatrice's affection. Dogberry and Verges approach Leonato with news of prisoners, but fail to explain the danger clearly before he leaves for church.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Claudio interrupts the marriage ceremony to reject Hero as unchaste. Don Pedro supports the accusation, Don John reinforces it, and Hero denies having spoken to anyone at her window. She faints, and Leonato initially shares the men's judgment. Beatrice defends her, the friar reads innocence in her response, and Benedick suspects Don John's malice. The friar advises that Hero be hidden and reported dead to provoke remorse and protect her while the matter is investigated. Alone together, Benedick and Beatrice acknowledge their love, but she asks him to kill Claudio over Hero's dishonour; he agrees to issue a challenge. The Watch's evidence exposes the plot during the prisoners' examination. Despite Dogberry's verbal confusion, the Sexton understands and goes to Leonato.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Leonato and Antonio demand satisfaction from Claudio, and Benedick issues his own challenge. Borachio's confession finally makes Claudio and Don Pedro recognize their error. Still believing Hero dead, Claudio accepts Leonato's terms: clear her name, honour her at the tomb and marry a supposed niece. The memorial song and epitaph enact his penance. Meanwhile Benedick and Beatrice continue their courtship and receive news of the discovery. At the promised marriage, the veiled woman proves to be Hero. Beatrice and Benedick's written declarations expose their love despite their denials, and they agree to marry as well. Benedick reconciles with Claudio and calls for a dance before the ceremonies. Don John's capture is reported, with punishment left for tomorrow.
